_comment: THE VERBAL FORMS of each edition (kb/Work PB5449, decision PB5448 point 3): a unit of unnumbered text disposed
`not-a-rule` (a cross-reference or data) is refused when any of its sentences holds one of these, since a form that
states a requirement, a permission or a defined result is the shape of a rule (text_units.guard_refusal). Each is a
case-insensitive regular expression over one sentence. 2023 defines its verbal forms in its Introduction ('shall' a
requirement, 'may' a permission; front matter, which cite.py has no locator for) and 2002 alike; 1985 defines none, its
syntax rules being those that 'define or clarify how the statement must be written' (§1985:IV.3.1), so 'must' is
1985's. The list is widened by the
misses kb/Work PB479's design review found: the function-type sentences (76 in the 2023 text, none in a row when
measured), 'is undefined', 'is unpredictable', 'implementor-defined', 'is treated as', 'is equivalent to'.
A lead-in is not guarded: its words are carried by its list's rows.
